name: SumMe
annotations: User-selected temporal intervals; human summary duration 5–15% of source
granularity: Temporal intervals mapped to original frames
split: No original canonical learning split; later random 80/20 canonical, augmented, and transfer protocols
license: Not independently verified; repository MIT license must not be applied to source videos
availability: Institutional archive cited; full archive download and integrity not verified in this run
preprocessing: Later pipelines: 2 fps, original-frame index mapping, KTS, usually 15% budget. These are method conventions, not native annotations.
features: Later paper-author packages: GoogLeNet pool5 HDF5 (2 fps, 1024-D) and MSVA I3D RGB/flow; original dataset release has no deep tensors. See docs/03-datasets.md. ResNet-101 and VideoMAE ready-made tensors not independently verified.
leakage_risks: Small corpus; external feature pretraining contamination unknown; do not use human-derived HDF5 fields for unsupervised checkpoint selection
limitations: Mean-user and max-user F1 are incompatible; source durations and checksums were not remeasured

name: TVSum / TVSum50
annotations: 1–5 importance rating for every 2-second unit; 1000 video-level responses
summary_format: Importance scores; reference keyshots require decoding
split: No original canonical learning split; later random 80/20 and five-split conventions
metrics: Kendall tau / Spearman rho for score ranking (later diagnostic)
license: Video source release identifies Creative Commons CC-BY 3.0; code and derived features need their own license checks
availability: Official README advertises hosted videos and URLs; author download directory is canonical. Full archive not downloaded.
preprocessing: Original annotation uses 2-second units; later KTS reference construction changes the protocol
features: Later paper-author packages: GoogLeNet pool5 HDF5 (2 fps, 1024-D) and MSVA I3D RGB/flow; original dataset release has no deep tensors. See docs/03-datasets.md. ResNet-101 and VideoMAE ready-made tensors not independently verified.
leakage_risks: Titles were visible during annotation; test reference scores must not tune models; public web-video contamination unknown
limitations: Do not equate raw ratings with binary user summaries or mix original units and shared-KTS references

name: OVP / VSUMM Open Video subset
task: Static keyframe summarization; auxiliary training for later temporal methods
duration: Published range 1–4 minutes; author README approximately 75 minutes total
split: No canonical split; later LSTM work uses all 50 as auxiliary training data
metrics: Content-matched keyframe precision, recall and F1 in later seqDPP protocol
availability: Author README links dataset, user-summary and evaluation archives; archive bytes not fetched in this run
preprocessing: Native MPEG-1, 30 fps, 352x240; oracle keyframe-to-score conversions are method-derived labels
features: seqDPP author Fisher/saliency/context bundle; later GoogLeNet derivatives advertised, current download not verified
leakage_risks: Derived oracle labels introduce human supervision; avoid treating auxiliary label transfer as unsupervised training
limitations: Content-matched still-frame metrics are not temporal-overlap F1; no dense native importance curve

name: YouTube / VSUMM web-video corpus
task: Static keyframe summarization; auxiliary training for later temporal methods
domain: Cartoons, news, sports, commercials, TV, home videos
duration: Published range 1–10 minutes/video; current archive not remeasured
split: Original release 50 videos; seqDPP/LSTM use a 39-video non-cartoon subset
metrics: Content-matched keyframe precision, recall and F1 in later seqDPP protocol
availability: Author release links web-video archive and user summaries; no byte integrity verification in this run
preprocessing: Name exact 50-video release or 39-video non-cartoon subset; derived oracle conversion must be documented
features: seqDPP Fisher/saliency/context bundle for 39-video subset; later GoogLeNet derivatives advertised but not downloaded
leakage_risks: Same videos may be reused by different auxiliary bundles; labels remain human-derived after conversion
limitations: Not the YouTube Highlights dataset; temporal F1 and static matching are incompatible

name: VideoXum
task: Cross-modal visual and textual video summarization
annotations: 10 visual summary masks per video; event-caption text; 140010 visual/text pairs
annotators: 10 visual summaries per video; text references are shared caption lists, not ten independent texts
granularity: Uniform 1-fps visual positions; temporal event captions
summary_format: Binary visual mask plus textual summary
license: Official Hugging Face dataset card: Apache-2.0; this does not relicense underlying ActivityNet/YouTube videos
availability: Official Hugging Face annotations and features advertised; raw video bytes not bundled
preprocessing: 1 fps; author evaluator commit 11bd4fe3 uses threshold at floor(0.15*N) with >=, selecting floor(0.15*N)+1 unique positions and possibly more ties. No KTS/knapsack. Correlation compares scores with mean-annotator ratings, not per-user correlation then averaging.
features: Official BLIP and fine-tuned VT-CLIP ViT-B/16 archives; VT-CLIP is not generic frozen CLIP
leakage_risks: ActivityNet overlap and upstream video-language pretraining contamination unknown; keep dataset partitions when fine-tuning VT-CLIP
limitations: Cross-modal, visual-only and textual metrics answer different questions; native frame selection differs from SumMe/TVSum

name: CoSum / Co-Sum
annotations: Query-related selected shots; reference pools majority selections
availability: Official repository has URLs, preprocessed shot indices and annotations; raw videos not durably hosted
preprocessing: Use supplied shot indices and declared subdivision of long shots
features: Paper descriptors: CENTRIST, Dense-SIFT, HSV moments; ready-made tensors not independently verified
leakage_risks: Query-group and cross-video co-occurrence exposure is part of the method; do not call it a single-video setting
limitations: 51 instances does not guarantee 51 distinct currently retrievable files; mAP is not temporal F1

name: UT Egocentric / UTE
domain: Uncontrolled daily life from head-mounted cameras
annotations: Important regions; reusable temporal user skims are not supplied by the original release
annotators: 4 camera wearers; annotation worker count not independently verified
summary_format: Original summaries evaluated by a human study
split: Four public test videos; leave-one-video-out important-region experiments are method-specific
license: Registration required; no general permissive data license independently verified
availability: Official page advertises 1.4-GB blurred-face video package and important-region annotations
preprocessing: Looxcie, 15 fps, 320x480; faces blurred in public media
features: No first-party deep tensor bundle independently verified
leakage_risks: QFVS and VideoSET reuse these same videos: derivative annotations are not new independent data
limitations: Six of ten recorded videos withheld for privacy; source warns summary evaluation needs a new human study

name: VideoSET annotation layer for UTE
task: Text-based evaluation of extractive visual summaries
domain: Four UTE daily-life videos within the larger VideoSET release
duration: Same UTE media; full VideoSET release covers about 40 hours / 11 videos
annotations: One factual sentence per 5-second segment; 3 reference text summaries/video
annotators: 3 summary references per video; segment annotation worker count not independently verified
split: No universal split; later UTE subset work uses leave-one-video-out
availability: Official project advertises annotation ZIP; raw UTE media remains separate
preprocessing: Map selected 5-second segments to their captions; original UTE evaluation uses 24 segments / 2 minutes
features: Annotation layer does not constitute visual feature release
leakage_risks: Shares UTE media with QFVS; captions used at test time change available supervision
limitations: Full VideoSET also has Disneyworld videos and TV episodes; this row deliberately counts only UTE subset

name: QFVS (Sharghi et al., CVPR 2017)
annotations: 48 concept tags; 46 queries per video; three user summaries per query-video pair; 5-second shot concept vectors
annotators: 3 workers per shot for concept tags (union); 3 student summary annotators
summary_format: Query-specific shot sets; unconstrained and 10/20-shot budgeted references
availability: Paper and UTE source available; original QFVS project endpoint failed to fetch in this audit; current annotation download not independently verified
preprocessing: Five sampled frames/shot during tagging; native concept metric uses semantic tags, not temporal overlap
features: Paper uses SentiBank-derived frame descriptors plus context; released tensor availability not independently verified
leakage_risks: Concept tags are evaluation annotations; reuse during model optimization changes supervision. UTE/VideoSET share media.
limitations: 46 queries per video, not 46 unique videos; 48 is concept-vocabulary size. Query summaries are distinct from native UTE annotations.

name: EgoSum+gaze
duration: Over 15 hours total; 15 minutes to 1.5 hours/video (paper)
annotations: Gaze plus wearer-selected semantic event blocks
annotators: 5 wearers; one wearer reference per video
availability: Official project and paper available; no public raw download linked by project
preprocessing: Gaze calibration and gaze-based subshot construction required
features: Paper uses R-CNN features; downloadable tensor bundle not independently verified
leakage_risks: Wearer-specific gaze/preferences; subject separation must be disclosed
limitations: Distinct media and annotation layer from UTE or QFVS; no universal 15% budget

name: SummScreen
videos: Not applicable: text-only release; 26851 episode records in final paper
duration: Not reported as media duration; mean source length 7605.4 tokens (FD), 6420.7 (TMS)
availability: Official repository links tokenized and untokenized archives; no video bytes
preprocessing: Recover final splits in untokenized archive by matching filenames to tokenized release; extra filtered records are present
features: Text; no native visual feature bundle
leakage_risks: Shows recur across splits; public transcripts and recaps may appear in language-model pretraining
limitations: Not a visual-skim benchmark. Final paper counts 4348 FD + 22503 TMS = 26851; do not copy rounded/earlier 26915 as exact.

name: SummScreen3D
domain: Five TV soap-opera shows; SummScreen-TMS derivative
annotations: Video/audio, transcripts, captions and multiple source recaps; 1.53 summaries/episode on average
annotators: Existing recap authors; number not reported
split: 3983 training episodes (derived: 4575-296-296), expanded to 5199 episode-summary pairs; 296 validation; 296 test
availability: Official repository has transcripts, summaries, closed captions, split files and video downloader; full media retrieval not tested
preprocessing: Shot detection and closed-caption/transcript alignment; keep all references of one episode in its assigned split
features: Paper describes multimodal extraction; ready-made tensor availability not independently verified
leakage_risks: Shares episodes and text with SummScreen; multiple references must not create episode leakage; model pretraining contamination unknown
limitations: Video-to-text evaluation differs from temporal extractive F1. 5199 counts training pairs, not unique videos.

name: ActivityNet-QA
duration: Mean 180 seconds (paper); total/range not independently verified
annotators: 10 QA pairs/video; unique annotator count not reported
availability: Official repository supplies QA annotations/evaluation; obtain ActivityNet media separately
preprocessing: Follow question/answer split identifiers and source-video mapping
features: Original work extracts VGG-16 fc7 and C3D fc7; repository tensor release not independently verified
leakage_risks: Shared ActivityNet parent corpus can overlap other benchmark training; QA labels are human supervision
limitations: No keyshot, importance or summary-duration labels; auxiliary understanding dataset only

name: Ego4D
task: Egocentric perception, episodic memory and other benchmark tasks
domain: Daily-life first-person video across locations and participants
videos: Not reported here: version-specific manifest required
duration: Official landing page: 3670 hours; documentation/repository use other version-dependent rounded totals
annotations: Narrations and task-specific perception annotations; no single native generic-summary reference layer
annotators: Task-dependent; not one common summary-annotator count
granularity: Task-dependent clips, narrations, moments and trajectories
metrics: Task-specific retrieval, localization, forecasting and perception metrics
license: Ego4D license agreement and approval required; licensed data/annotation access
availability: Credential-gated download via official CLI; no download attempted
preprocessing: Pin release version, benchmark, video_uid and selected modality/subset
features: Official CLI supports a features package; feature model and release must be checked per manifest
leakage_risks: Participant/video overlap and derived dataset overlap require explicit checks; narratives are annotation supervision
limitations: Do not infer a native summarization benchmark from egocentric coverage; counts differ by release

name: YouTube Highlights / Domain-specific Personal Video Highlights
domain: Dog, gymnastics, parkour, skating, skiing, surfing
videos: Not independently verified: distinguish harvested vlist.json and selected vlist_sel.json
duration: Not independently verified for a pinned selected manifest
annotations: Edited-video matched/unmatched/borderline clips; separate MTurk highlight votes
annotators: MTurk vote counts in mturk_label.json; unique annotator count not verified
split: Official train/test tight/loose label groups; selected subset differs from harvested set
availability: Official repository supplies clip/label manifests and legacy media downloader; current video availability not tested
preprocessing: Preserve clip frame indices, tight/loose group and harvested/selected subset; labels 1/-1/0 have distinct meanings
features: Primary code release; ready-made modern deep features not independently verified
leakage_risks: Raw and edited pairs must remain grouped; highlight matching supplies weak human-edit supervision
limitations: Not the 50-video VSUMM YouTube corpus and not a generic 15% summary benchmark

name: TVR / TV show Retrieval
duration: Video count is paper-rounded 21.8K; exact release duration not independently verified
annotations: 109K natural-language queries with temporal windows; query modality types
annotators: Not reported here; qualification and verification described by primary paper
granularity: Localized temporal windows inside video clips
summary_format: Not applicable: queries localize moments, not episode recaps
split: Use official release split; exact counts not independently verified here
metrics: Moment retrieval recall at temporal IoU thresholds
availability: Official project linked by primary paper; media and feature retrieval not verified in this run
preprocessing: Keep subtitle/video alignment and query type; TVC caption extension is a separate task
features: Version-specific visual/subtitle features; not independently verified
leakage_risks: Shared TV sources and TVC captions require overlap checks with other TV benchmarks
limitations: TVR and TVC are retrieval/captioning resources, not automatically summarization datasets; use a named summary annotation extension for summaries

name: MoSu (Most Replayed Multimodal Video Summarization)
task: Multimodal importance prediction and extractive summarization using behavioral targets
annotations: YouTube Most Replayed statistics: 100 initial bins, bias-corrected and aligned to frames; derived gt_score and gt_summary
annotators: Aggregated viewer behavior, not explicit summary annotations; inclusion threshold is over 50000 views, not a verified distinct-annotator count
granularity: Replay curve aligned to 1-second feature positions; stored change points
summary_format: Importance curve and derived binary summary
license: Official dataset card: CC-BY-4.0; source YouTube media rights remain separate; repository code MIT
availability: Official metadata, ground truth, feature HDF5 and splits advertised; no binary archives downloaded in this run
preprocessing: English or YouTube-translated transcripts and audio required; aligned visual, text and audio features at 1-second intervals
features: Official CLIP ViT-L/14, RoBERTa-base and AST HDF5; each video matrix N x 768; card advertises about 40 GB per modality and 136 GB total
leakage_risks: YouTube8M-derived source overlap with other web corpora requires source-ID deduplication; replay statistics and pretrained encoders introduce separate provenance issues
limitations: Replays measure engagement rather than independently judged summary completeness; raw media retrieved by source IDs may disappear; derived binary targets depend on decoding
metrics: mAP50 and mAP15 under Mr. HiSum 5-second segment protocol

name: TripleSumm long-video test set
domain: Films/documentaries, tutorials, full sports matches and multilingual talk shows
duration: Mean 4224 seconds (70.4 minutes); standard deviation 1263.6 seconds; range 2413–7207 seconds
annotations: Most Replayed behavioral importance targets using the MoSu preprocessing approach
annotators: Not reported; behavioral targets, not individually authored summary references
granularity: Replay statistics aligned to temporal feature positions
split: 50 evaluation-only videos; direct transfer from MoSu-trained model
availability: Paper describes the test set; dedicated public media/annotation artifact not independently verified
preprocessing: Paper Appendix B.6; MoSu behavioral-target processing applied to longer videos
leakage_risks: Different domains do not by themselves establish absence of source or encoder-pretraining overlap
limitations: Only 50 videos; behavior-based targets; artifact access and independent reproduction unresolved
